editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a tiny wooden shack on a windy beach with a complete stranger. That is exactly where you find Roy, a lonely bird watcher who is just one rare bird away from finishing his life goal. He spends his time talking to a picture of his ex-wife until a messy, bloody man named Dave bursts through the door to escape a storm. At first, you will feel the tension because you do not know if Dave is dangerous or just unlucky. But as they share tea and sandwiches, you start to see a weird friendship grow between these two broken men. It feels like a slow-burn drama that slowly turns into a scary game of cat and mouse.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the two leads keep you guessing about who is actually the bad guy. The pacing is slow, which might bore some people, but it builds the stress perfectly. If you like stories where the location is small and the mood is heavy, you will love this. It is a great pick for fans of psychological thrillers who want something different.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that Dave is actually a dangerous killer on the run from the police. After pretending to be a friend, he turns violent. Roy tries to survive, but the movie ends in a sad way. The police finally arrive, but it is too late to save Roy from the tragedy. You realize that the friendly bond they built was just a trick Dave used to keep Roy quiet and trapped.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and twist endings.
